subject: Issues with error and periodogram help

messages.author: 2a5dcfbe2fdafe70
messages.subject: Issues with error and periodogram help
parts:
Hi Chris,

I have a set of telemetry data for bats that I used to get spatial location estimates using the 'razimuth' package created by Gerber et al., 2018.

I then followed methodology from Rizzuto et al., 2021 to incorporate the error estimates into ctmm. I successfully incorporated the error estimates into a column called "COV.x.y" and when using the ctmm.guess function, stated error to be true. However when plotting my data, it does not appear to show error ellipses and gives the notice of "DOP values missing. Assuming DOP=1". I am concerned it is not recognizing or incorporating the error data. How do I confirm and/or force the function to recognize my COV.x.y column as my error column?

I have attached a .csv file and reproducible example for a subset of my individuals. I've included 1 individual that is giving me trouble in this dataset (likely due to low amounts of data).

Additionally, I was hoping to share in confidence the full data set as I am trying to understand if I need to incorporate periodicity into these models. The data was collected on bats during the maternity season that are returning to a nightly roost and data was only collected at night. Should I be looking at periodograms? Thank you for your help!


Best,

Amber Litterer

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Issues with error and periodogram help
parts:
Hi Amber,

Sorry for the delay. Looking at the referenced Rmd file, I don't know if there is something fancy going on with that dplyr code that I can't immediately see, but at least in your script I can see that there are a bunch of missing pieces. Here's one method that should work:
  1. In your working projection, you need to calculate the error ellipse covariance matrices, which have the unique components "COV.x.x","COV.x.y","COV.y.y" in ctmm name format. You need all three of these values for every location estimate to make an error ellipse.
  2. After you have imported your data into ctmm and it's in the same projection, then you make the data appear calibrated with uere(DATA) <- 1 though the error information will be bogus thus far.
  3. Then you can copy over the  "COV.x.x","COV.x.y","COV.y.y" columns.
  4. Then there's one final column that you may or may not need, which is the approximate error radius: DATA$VAR.xy <- (DATA$COV.x.x+DATA$COV.y.y)/2
That should leave you with a dataset that registers as calibrated with the correct error ellipse and radius information.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Issues with error and periodogram help
parts:
I forgot to answer your periodicity question. If they are roosting at night, then the better model is probably just to work with the daily foraging data in a stationary model. Periodic location models would be more interesting if they were going to specific locations during the day. You can try and see, though.

Best,
Chris
